newsitem.title: USA: U.S. officials set Nazi compensation claim deadline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. officials set Nazi compensation claim deadline.

text.p: Justice Department officials on Thursday said U.S. citizens have another month to add to the 250 claims seeking compensation from the German government for Nazi concentration camp survivors.
"We are racing against time to compensate them," Attorney General Janet Reno said of the programme unveiled in June. She announced a Feb. 23 deadline for any more claims.
Under an agreement between the U.S. and German governments any U.S citizen who was interned in a Nazi concentration camp during the Second World War can file a claim for reparation.

Delissa Ridgway, head of the Foreign Claims Settlement Commission, a Justice Department agency administering the programme, said 250 claims already had been submitted but she did not know how many would be eligible for compensation. She said the claims would be checked with international records.
The U.S.-German agreement applies to both civilians and military personnel who were U.S. citizens at the time of their internment in the Nazi camps.
Ridgway was unable to estimate how many U.S. citizens had been placed in the camps and were still alive. She said the amount of money would vary on a case-by-case basis.
Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, said in response to Reno's announcement, "To set a deadline when we don't have all the facts would be premature."
